requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.

hunches.claim: The tests never verify that an ordinary, undecorated composite resolver receives ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. The only composite-resolver test predecorates the resolver and skips generated-source checks, so it exercises only attribute suppression; removing the normal emission would leave REQ-2297's composite-resolver path untested.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/CompositeResolverTemplate.cs:29 delete-statement: this.Write("[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]\r\n"); -> removed; expected to survive because AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage runs only MessagePackGenerator, while CompositeResolverAlreadyExcludedByUserStillCompiles takes the UserDeclaredExcludeFromCodeCoverage branch and uses SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck.

refused.what: Choosing between reading A and reading B of REQ-2297
refused.why: The AI will not pick: 3 of 3 independent readers found two readings: A: Unconditionally apply `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` to every type emitted by the source generator, including formatters and resolvers, with no configuration setting; B: Unconditionally apply the attribute only to generated formatter types, leaving other generated types such as resolvers undecorated; the requirement says: 'Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open'. Reading A: Unconditionally apply `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` to every type emitted by the source generator, including formatters and resolvers, with no configuration setting. Code: Update all relevant formatter, string-key, enum, union, and resolver templates to emit the attribute (conditionally if needed for target-framework compatibility), and regenerate every affected verified snapshot; no opt-out API or MSBuild option is added. Reading B: Unconditionally apply the attribute only to generated formatter types, leaving other generated types such as resolvers undecorated. Code: Update the formatter-related templates, including string-key and enum/union formatters, but do not modify resolver or other non-formatter generation paths, so only formatter snapshots gain the attribute. Which one ships is a product decision, not a correctness question; both branches are built and reviewed with their own receipts, and a named human merges one.
